prompts.summary: Explore the repository and identify main components and commands
prompts.requires: read access to the repository and a shell
prompts.example: explore the structure and main modules

prompts.summary: Trace a flow and its dependencies through the code

prompts.example: trace the authentication and session flow

prompts.summary: Give a guided tour of the code or a concept for someone new to it
prompts.requires: The code, module or concept to explain and the reader's starting level
prompts.example: UND03: explain how the payment retry flow works to a new teammate

prompts.summary: Find official sources that fit the technical problem

prompts.summary: Summarize recent repository activity: commits, issues and pull requests

prompts.example: define acceptance criteria for full-text search

prompts.requires: alternatives to evaluate and project constraints

prompts.summary: Design API contracts, data models and compatibility

prompts.summary: Develop the remaining features in phases with tests and accessibility checks

prompts.summary: Prepare release, hosting, monitoring, backups and handover of a site or app

prompts.summary: Harden a website against common attacks and abuse

prompts.summary: Start a session: context, repository state, alignment and next tasks
prompts.requires: any folder; a managed repository adds the dossier, the tracker and the alignment check
prompts.example: SES01: start the session in this repository and propose the next tasks

prompts.summary: Close the session with memories, tracker and handoff updated
prompts.requires: state of the work done, defined next tasks and delivery destination
prompts.example: sb prompt SES02: close the session and ask for commit and push

prompts.summary: Stop the agent and hand the session over to another IDE or account
prompts.requires: the task in progress, the Git state of the checkout and the person's choice for uncommitted work
prompts.example: sb stop: I am at the end of my weekly limit, save the session so I can resume from another account

prompts.summary: Resume work stopped by a usage limit, importing it from another account
prompts.requires: the stopped work (MEM09 or MEM03 report, runner resume.json, branch or worktree) and the import method the person picks
prompts.example: SES04: the runner stopped for quota on the other account, import its work and continue the task

prompts.summary: Read memory, context and tracker of the current repository and list its tasks
prompts.requires: checkout of the open repository
prompts.example: sb prompt TRK01: load the repository context and list the ready tasks

prompts.summary: Complete the next ready task of the open repository
prompts.requires: planned task and acceptance criteria
prompts.example: run the next priority task that can be done autonomously

prompts.summary: Inspect the repo and find leftover tasks against the real code
prompts.requires: working tree, recent history and any backlog or notes
prompts.example: inspect the repo and detect leftover tasks

prompts.summary: Run ready autonomous tasks with the runner and record the outcome
prompts.requires: ready autonomous tasks, the desktop runner (scripts/runner.ps1) or the command line (run-ready-tasks.ps1, launcher) and the user's go-ahead for -Run
prompts.example: TRK04: run the ready autonomous tasks, follow the run and record the outcome

prompts.summary: Unblock blocked tasks: verify the real reason, then make them autonomous

prompts.summary: Prepare tasks for unattended runs, one at a time

prompts.example: TRK08: make the next tasks autonomous one by one, stop at 5, then start the queue
